sources.observed_text: SQLite documents reader end marks and says a checkpoint must stop before overwriting pages beyond any current reader's end mark; PASSIVE can remain incomplete with concurrent readers or writers.
sources.review_interpretation: The end-mark constraint motivating the proposed relation is known prior art. These experiments do not establish that mechanism as novel.

sources.observed_text: PASSIVE attempts as much checkpoint work as possible without waiting; outputs include log and checkpointed frame counts, and concurrent readers/writers can leave work unfinished.
sources.review_interpretation: This explains API semantics. It does not support a claim that reader lifecycle scheduling improves net cost.

sources.retrieval_evidence: Project-saved Crossref metadata check (2026-11-04) identifies Zhu, Hu, and Wang, 'Asynchronous and Adaptive Checkpoint for WAL-based Data Storage Systems' (2023); no abstract/full text was available in that check.
sources.review_interpretation: An adjacent adaptive checkpoint policy is known. Its exact relation to application-visible SQLite reader lifecycle signals remains unresolved without full text; novelty is not established.

scope: Targeted check of known SQLite WAL semantics and the nearest cited adaptive-checkpoint work; not a comprehensive literature review.
